alignment.note: Greek ὑμεῖς and Syriac ܐܢܬܘܢ supply the emphatic independent pronoun 'you (yourselves)'; the Vulgate folds this emphasis into the reflexive vosmetipsos and provides no separate subject pronoun, a function of Latin's pro-drop syntax.
ἑαυτούς / ܢܦܫܟܘܢ / vosmetipsos — the parenthetical transliteration (he'autous) is treated as part of the same reflexive lexeme.

Greek ὑμᾶς and Vulgate vos render the accusative object 'you'; the Syriac encodes this object pronominally as the suffix on the verb ܢܫܠܡܘܢܟܘܢ ('they will hand you over'), so no discrete object token appears in the Peshitta.

Greek εἰς συνέδρια and Latin in consiliis ('into councils/sanhedrins', plural) use a preposition + plural noun; Syriac ܠܕܝܢܐ employs the lamadh-prefixed singular 'to the tribunal/judgement', a collective rendering that flattens the institutional plural of the Greek συνέδριον.

Greek καὶ εἰς συναγωγὰς and Latin et in synagogis coordinate with a conjunction plus preposition plus plural noun; Syriac compresses conjunction, preposition, plural noun, and a 3mp possessive suffix into the single form ܘܒܟܢܘܫܬܗܘܢ ('and in their synagogues'), adding the possessive 'their' not present in Greek or Latin.

Greek δαρήσεσθε ('you will be beaten/flogged', from δέρω) and Syriac ܬܬܢܓܕܘܢ ('you will be scourged/dragged') denote corporal punishment; the Vulgate vapulabitis uses the deponent vapulo 'to be thrashed', a colloquial Latin equivalent with the same passive sense.
καὶ / ܘ- (prefixed on ܘܩܕܡ) / et — coordinating conjunction.
ἐπὶ / ܩܕܡ / ante — 'before, in the presence of'; the Syriac conjunction and preposition are fused in ܘܩܕܡ.

Greek (ἡγεμόνων καὶ βασιλέων, 'governors and kings') and Latin (præsides et reges) list governors first, then kings; the Peshitta inverts the order to ܡܠܟܐ ܘܗܓܡܘܢܐ ('kings and governors'), a word-order divergence placing the higher office first.
ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ / ܡܛܠܬܝ / propter me — 'on account of me'; Syriac fuses preposition and 1cs suffix into a single form.

Greek εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς and Latin in testimonium illis use preposition + noun + separate dative pronoun ('for a testimony to them'); the Syriac ܠܣܗܕܘܬܗܘܢ collapses lamadh-preposition, noun, and 3mp suffix into one word, expressing 'their testimony / a testimony to them' synthetically.
